newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Beef, wool, log prices drive NZ Jun qtr PPI down.
newsitem.headline: Beef, wool, log prices drive NZ Jun qtr PPI down.

text.p: Decreases in beef, wool and log prices drove the New Zealand Producers Price Index lower in the June quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
Output price levels of goods and services sold by New Zealand industries fell on average by 0.2 percent in the quarter, following a 0.3 percent rise in the March quarter.
SNZ said the quarterly fall continued a trend of low or negative changes in the outputs index.
Output price levels for the June quarter were 0.4 percent higher than those recorded a year earlier, down on the annual rise to the March quarter of 1.0 percent.

Input price levels of goods and services, excluding wages and depreciation, purchased by New Zealand industries also fell 0.2 percent in the quarter, following a 0.4 percent rise in the March quarter.
The fall was the first since the March 1994 quarter.
The annual rise in inputs was 0.5 percent, against an annual rise to the March quarter of 0.9 percent.
SNZ pointed to decreases in beef, wool and log prices as the main factor behind the 0.2 percent quarterly falls in inputs and outputs.

It said beef and other agricultural product prices were influenced by the bovine spongiform encepholopathy (BSE) scare. Cattle prices fell 14 percent in the quarter, while sheep and lamb prices rose nearly three percent. Overall, the livestock and cropping index, which contributes to the agriculture outputs index, fell 5.2 percent. Wool prices fell nine percent.

SNZ said sawlog and pulp log prices were lower due to low world prices and high stocks. This impacted on the forestry and logging outputs index and several input indexes, including paper, printing and publishing inputs, which fell 4.5 percent.

The agriculture output price index fell 1.7 percent, and contributed most to the 0.2 percent quarterly fall in output prices. Forestry and logging, with a 7.7 percent quarterly fall, provided the next most significant contribution.

The textiles, apparel and leather output price index also decreased, by two percent, while construction rose 0.6 percent. SNZ said this rise, on the back of higher house construction prices, provided the main offset to the overall quarterly fall.
Crude oil prices fell this quarter, after rising in the previous quarter due to higher world prices. This caused the chemicals, petroleum and plastics inputs index to fall.
